input.question: What are the contemporary general feelings / official teachings in Japan regarding their involvement in WWII?
input.ground_truth: I went to the Hiroshima Museum a few years ago. The history there was a complete white-wash. Every act by Japan was an "incident". e.g. The incident at the Marco Polo bridge, the incident at Pearl Harbor brought the US into the war. Even the Rape of Nanking was completely glossed over.

Question: What are the contemporary general feelings / official teachings in Japan regarding their involvement in WWII?

Okay! Imagine you and your friends played a big game a long time ago that wasn’t very nice, and some people got really hurt. Now, some grown-ups in Japan remember that game (which is World War II) and feel sad or sorry about what happened. They talk about it in school and on TV, and they try to make sure it doesn’t happen again.

The teachers and the government in Japan tell kids and everyone that what happened was very bad and that they want to make sure it never happens again. They also say that Japan wants to be friends with other countries now. But some people in other countries still feel upset about what happened, so Japan tries to be very careful and polite when talking about it.

So, in Japan, people mostly feel sorry and want to be good friends now, but they also remember the bad things that happened and promise to never do them again.
